title: 13  Liquidity
text:
13.1 Measuring Illiquidity
Following Chapter 13 of Bali et al. (2016), we ask whether less liquid stocks earn higher subsequent returns. We estimate Amihud illiquidity from legacy CRSP daily data and examine the Pástor–Stambaugh liquidity factors separately. The former measures how much an individual stock’s price moves for a given trading volume. The latter measure marketwide liquidity and exposure to changes in it.
The measure of Amihud (2002) averages the absolute daily return per million dollars traded. For a window of \(k\) calendar months ending in formation month \(t\), let \(\mathcal D_{i,t}^{(k)}\) be the usable trading days and let \(D_{i,t}^{(k)}\) be their count.
\[
\operatorname{Illiq}_{i,t}^{(k)}
=\frac{1}{D_{i,t}^{(k)}}\sum_{d\in\mathcal D_{i,t}^{(k)}}
\frac{|R_{i,d}|}{P_{i,d}Q_{i,d}/10^6}.
\tag{13.1}\]
\(R_{i,d}\) is the decimal CRSP return, \(P_{i,d}\) is the closing trade price, and \(Q_{i,d}\) is the number of shares traded. We require a finite return and strictly positive price and volume. A negative CRSP price denotes a bid–ask average, which BEM exclude for this measure. The minimum counts for the one-, three-, six-, and twelve-month windows are 15, 50, 100, and 200 usable days. We also use \(\log(1+\operatorname{Illiq}_{i,t}^{(k)})\), which reduces the influence of large values without changing their ranks.
import polars as pl

from era_pl import load_parquet
from eap_pl import build_book_to_market, build_momentum, build_sizes, monthly_panel

keys = ["permno", "month"]
first = pl.date(1963, 6, 1)
last = pl.date(2012, 11, 1)
minimum_days = {1: 15, 3: 50, 6: 100, 12: 200}
raw = {f"illiq{k}": f"`illiq{k}`" for k in minimum_days}
logged = {f"log_{term}": f"`log_{term}`" for term in raw}
measures = raw | logged

sizes = build_sizes()
book_to_market = build_book_to_market(sizes).select(*keys, "bm")
stock_months = (
    load_parquet("msf", "crsp")
    .filter(pl.col("date").is_between(first, last.dt.offset_by("1mo").dt.month_end()))
    .select("permno", month=pl.col("date").dt.month_start(),
            stock_return=pl.when(pl.col("ret").is_finite()).then(pl.col("ret")))
)
monthly_factors = (
    load_parquet("factors_monthly", "ff")
    .select("rf", month=pl.col("date").dt.month_start(),
            mkt=100 * pl.col("mktrf"), smb=100 * pl.col("smb"), hml=100 * pl.col("hml"))
    .collect()
)
unadjusted = (
    stock_months.collect()
    .join(monthly_factors.select("month", "rf"), on="month", validate="m:1")
    .select("permno", month=pl.col("month").dt.offset_by("-1mo"),
            unadjusted=100 * (pl.col("stock_return") - pl.col("rf")))
)
formation = (
    monthly_panel(sizes, first, last)
    .join(book_to_market, on=keys, how="left", validate="1:1")
    .join(build_momentum(first, last).select(*keys, "mom"), on=keys, how="left", validate="1:1")
    .join(stock_months.select(*keys, rev=100 * pl.col("stock_return")).collect(),
          on=keys, how="left", validate="1:1")
    .join(unadjusted, on=keys, how="left", validate="1:1")
)
Pool the daily ratios and counts over each window so that each usable day receives equal weight. The rolling windows use elapsed calendar months. Months without a usable day contribute zero to the sum and count.
daily = load_parquet("dsf", "crsp").filter(
    pl.col("date").is_between(first.dt.offset_by("-11mo"), last.dt.month_end()),
    pl.col("ret").is_finite(),
    pl.col("prc").is_finite(),
    pl.col("vol").is_finite(),
    pl.col("prc") > 0,
    pl.col("vol") > 0,
)
monthly = (
    daily.with_columns(
        month=pl.col("date").dt.month_start(),
        daily_illiq=pl.col("ret").abs() / (pl.col("prc") * pl.col("vol") / 1e6),
    )
    .group_by(keys)
    .agg(total=pl.col("daily_illiq").sum(), days=pl.len())
    .collect()
    .join(formation.select(keys), on=keys, how="full", coalesce=True, validate="1:1")
    .with_columns(pl.col("total", "days").fill_null(0))
    .sort(keys)
)

panel = formation
for k, minimum in minimum_days.items():
    window = (
        monthly.rolling(index_column="month", period=f"{k}mo", group_by="permno")
        .agg(pl.col("total", "days").sum())
        .select(*keys, pl.when(pl.col("days") >= minimum)
                .then(pl.col("total") / pl.col("days")).alias(f"illiq{k}"))
    )
    panel = panel.join(window, on=keys, how="left", validate="1:1")
panel = panel.with_columns(pl.col(*raw).log1p().name.prefix("log_"))

title: 13  Liquidity
text:
13.3 Illiquidity and Stock Returns
We use next-month excess returns, including the delisting treatment in Section 7.2. One panel of Table 13.4 uses unadjusted CRSP returns to show the effect of including delistings. The risk models are the four-factor model in Equation 11.2 and that model augmented by the short-term reversal factor in Equation 12.2.

from io import StringIO
from pathlib import Path
import re

from eap_pl import format_fit, hac
from eap_pl._portfolios import assign_portfolio, portfolio_months, spread


def archived_factor(filename, name):
    rows = re.findall(r"(?m)^\s*(\d{6},[^\r\n]+)", Path(filename).read_text())
    return (
        pl.read_csv(StringIO("\n".join(rows)), has_header=False,
                    new_columns=["ym", name], schema_overrides={name: pl.String})
        .select(
            pl.col(name).str.strip_chars().cast(pl.Float64).replace([-99.99, -999], None),
            month=(pl.col("ym").cast(pl.String) + "01").str.to_date("%Y%m%d"),
        )
    )


factors = (
    monthly_factors.drop("rf")
    .join(archived_factor("data/momentum-202412.csv", "mom_factor"), on="month", validate="1:1")
    .join(archived_factor("data/st-reversal-202412.csv", "str_factor"), on="month", validate="1:1")
)
ff = "mkt + smb + hml"
ffc = f"{ff} + mom_factor"
ffcstr = f"{ffc} + str_factor"
models = {"Return": "1", "FFC α": ffc, "FFCSTR α": ffcstr}


def factor_fit(series, weight, rhs):
    sample = (
        series.select(pl.col("month").dt.offset_by("1mo"), weight)
        .join(factors, on="month", how="left", validate="1:1")
        .drop_nulls(weight)
        .sort("month")
    )
    return hac(f"{weight} ~ {rhs}", sample)


def spread_statistics(series, weight, specifications):
    return {label: format_fit(factor_fit(series, weight, rhs), "Intercept")
            for label, rhs in specifications.items()}


13.3.1 Univariate Portfolio Analysis
We form monthly deciles using all eligible stocks with each measure, then compute equal- and value-weighted returns. Value weights use formation-month capitalization. The 10–1 portfolio buys the least liquid decile and sells the most liquid decile.

deciles = [str(i) for i in range(1, 11)]
characteristics = {"illiq12": raw["illiq12"], "log_illiq12": logged["log_illiq12"],
                   "beta": "Beta", "cap": "Market cap ($ millions)",
                   "bm": "`bm`", "mom": "`mom`", "rev": "`rev`"}
decile_results = {}
for term in raw:
    members = assign_portfolio(panel.filter(pl.col(term).is_finite()), term, 10, "month")
    metrics = [pl.col("unadjusted").mean().alias("EW unadjusted")]
    if term == "illiq12":
        metrics.extend(pl.col(col).mean().alias(label) for col, label in characteristics.items())
    decile_results[term] = portfolio_months(members, ["portfolio"], metrics)


means = (
    decile_results["illiq12"].group_by("portfolio")
    .agg(pl.col(*characteristics.values()).mean()).sort("portfolio")
)
show_table(pl.DataFrame([
    {"Characteristic": label, **dict(zip(deciles, means[label]))}
    for label in characteristics.values()
]))

for weight in ("EW", "EW unadjusted", "VW"):
    rows = []
    for term, label in raw.items():
        monthly = decile_results[term].rename({weight: "outcome"})
        means = monthly.group_by("portfolio").agg(pl.col("outcome").mean()).sort("portfolio")
        long_short = spread(monthly, 10, 1, "portfolio", "outcome")
        statistics = spread_statistics(long_short, "outcome", models)
        rows.append({"Sort variable": label, **dict(zip(deciles, means["outcome"])),
                     "10–1": statistics.pop("Return"), **statistics})
    show_table(pl.DataFrame(rows))

monthly = decile_results["illiq1"]
groups = monthly.partition_by("portfolio", as_dict=True)
fits = {str(i): factor_fit(groups[i,], "VW", ffcstr) for i in range(1, 11)}
fits["10–1"] = factor_fit(spread(monthly, 10, 1, "portfolio", "VW"), "VW", ffcstr)
terms = {"Intercept": "FFCSTR α", "mkt": "`mkt`", "smb": "`smb`", "hml": "`hml`",
         "mom_factor": "`mom_factor`", "str_factor": "`str_factor`"}
show_table(pl.DataFrame([
    {"Statistic": label, **{decile: format_fit(fit, term) for decile, fit in fits.items()}}
    for term, label in terms.items()
]))

13.3.2 Bivariate Portfolio Analysis
Each two-way sort uses stocks with both characteristics available. We form quintiles first on a control variable, then on twelve-month illiquidity. In dependent sorts, we calculate the second set of cutoffs within each control quintile. In independent sorts, we calculate both sets of cutoffs from the monthly cross-section and intersect the groups. The average column weights the available control cells equally within each month and illiquidity quintile.

from eap_pl import bivariate_months

quintiles = [f"Q{i}" for i in range(1, 6)]
group_labels = [*quintiles, "Average"]


def spread_by_control(monthly, weight):
    groups = monthly.partition_by("control", as_dict=True)
    averaged = monthly.group_by("month", "target").agg(
        pl.col(weight).mean(), pl.col("market").first(),
    )
    return {
        label: spread(group, 5, 1, "target", weight)
        for label, group in zip(group_labels, [*(groups[i,] for i in range(1, 6)), averaged])
    }


def two_way_spreads(pairs, dependent, model_overrides=None):
    model_overrides = model_overrides or {}
    rows = []
    for control, target, label in pairs:
        sample = panel.filter(pl.all_horizontal(pl.col(control, target).is_finite()))
        monthly = bivariate_months(sample, control, target, nyse=False, dependent=dependent)
        specifications = model_overrides.get(target, models)
        for weight in ("EW", "VW"):
            spreads = {group: spread_statistics(series, weight, specifications)
                       for group, series in spread_by_control(monthly, weight).items()}
            for statistic in specifications:
                rows.append({"Characteristic": label, "Weights": weight, "Statistic": statistic,
                             **{group: values[statistic] for group, values in spreads.items()}})
    return pl.DataFrame(rows)


size_sample = panel.filter(pl.all_horizontal(pl.col("cap", "illiq12").is_finite()))
size_groups = assign_portfolio(size_sample, "cap", 5, "month", label="control")
size_groups = assign_portfolio(size_groups, "illiq12", 5, ["month", "control"], label="target")
size_cells = portfolio_months(
    size_groups.drop_nulls(["control", "target"]), ["control", "target"],
    [pl.col("cap").mean().alias("size")],
)


def size_grid(value):
    grid = (
        size_cells.group_by("target", "control").agg(pl.col(value).mean())
        .with_columns(group=pl.format("Q{}", pl.col("control")))
        .pivot(on="group", index="target", values=value)
    )
    month_averages = (
        size_cells.group_by("month", "target").agg(pl.col(value).mean())
        .group_by("target").agg(pl.col(value).mean().alias("Average"))
    )
    return (
        grid.join(month_averages, on="target", validate="1:1")
        .sort("target")
        .select(pl.format("`illiq12` {}", pl.col("target")).alias("Portfolio"), *group_labels)
    )


size_spreads = {group: spread_statistics(series, "EW", models)
                for group, series in spread_by_control(size_cells, "EW").items()}
return_rows = [
    {"Portfolio": label, **{group: f"{value:.2f}" for group, value in zip(group_labels, values)}}
    for label, *values in size_grid("EW").iter_rows()
]
return_rows.extend(
    {"Portfolio": f"5–1 {statistic}", **{group: result[statistic] for group, result in size_spreads.items()}}
    for statistic in models
)
show_table(pl.DataFrame(return_rows))
show_table(size_grid("size").with_columns(pl.col(group_labels).round().cast(pl.Int64)))

        table["(1)"].alias(f"({i})") for i, table in enumerate(tables, 1)

title: 13  Liquidity
text:
13.4 Liquidity Factors
The stock-level liquidity measure of Pástor and Stambaugh (2003) captures the following day’s reversal after trading pressure. For each stock and month they estimate
\[
r_{i,d+1}-r_{M,d+1}
=\theta_{i,m}+\phi_{i,m}r_{i,d}
+\gamma_{i,m}\operatorname{sign}(r_{i,d}-r_{M,d})V_{i,d}
+\varepsilon_{i,d+1},
\tag{13.2}\]
where \(V_{i,d}\) is dollar volume in millions and both days fall in month \(m\). The fit requires at least 15 usable pairs. A more negative \(\widehat{\gamma}_{i,m}\) associates signed volume with a larger subsequent reversal.
The aggregate measure averages the estimated stock coefficients for the eligible stocks.
\[
\widehat{\gamma}_m=\frac{1}{N_m}\sum_{i=1}^{N_m}\widehat{\gamma}_{i,m}.
\tag{13.3}\]
The aggregation uses stocks with a price of $5 to $1,000 at the prior month-end. The plotted level scales the average by \(V_m/V_1\), using the total prior month-end capitalization of the eligible stocks and August 1962 as the base month. We use the authors’ December 2013 release, the same vintage used by BEM. The file comes with eap_pl and includes the aggregate level, innovations, and traded factor.

from plotnine_polars import aes

from eap_pl import load_pastor_stambaugh_2013

end = pl.date(2012, 12, 1)
liquidity = load_pastor_stambaugh_2013().filter(pl.col("date") <= end)
assert liquidity["date"].equals(pl.date_range(pl.date(1962, 8, 1), end, "1mo", eager=True))
assert liquidity.select(pl.all_horizontal(pl.col("level", "innovation").is_finite()).fill_null(False).all()).item()


def plot_liquidity(series, label):
    return (
        liquidity.ggplot(aes(x="date", y=series))
        .geom_hline(yintercept=0, color="#777777", size=0.45)
        .geom_line(color="#15627c", size=0.55)
        .scale_x_date(date_breaks="10 years", date_labels="%Y")
        .labs(x="Month", y=label)
        .theme_minimal()
        .add_theme(figure_size=(8.2, 3.25))
    )


plot_liquidity("level", "Aggregate liquidity")







Figure 13.1: Scaled aggregate market liquidity, August 1962 to December 2012 (BEM Figure 13.1)





To isolate liquidity innovations, Pástor and Stambaugh average the change in stock-level liquidity among stocks observed in both months and scale it by market capitalization for that set of stocks.
\[
\Delta\widehat{\gamma}_m =
\frac{V_m}{V_1}\frac{1}{N_m}
\sum_{i=1}^{N_m}(\widehat{\gamma}_{i,m}-\widehat{\gamma}_{i,m-1}).
\tag{13.4}\]
\[
\Delta\widehat{\gamma}_m =
a+b\,\Delta\widehat{\gamma}_{m-1}
+c\,\frac{V_{m-1}}{V_1}\widehat{\gamma}_{m-1}+u_m.
\tag{13.5}\]
\[
L_m=\frac{\widehat u_m}{100}.
\tag{13.6}\]

plot_liquidity("innovation", "Liquidity innovation")







Figure 13.2: Innovations in aggregate market liquidity, August 1962 to December 2012 (BEM Figure 13.2)





The traded factor compares stocks with high and low historical exposure to liquidity innovations. Pástor and Stambaugh estimate the exposure \(\beta_{i,L}\) from up to five years of monthly excess returns, requiring at least 36 observations.
\[
r_{i,m}^{e}=\alpha_i+\beta_{i,M}\mathrm{MKT}_m+
\beta_{i,S}\mathrm{SMB}_m+\beta_{i,H}\mathrm{HML}_m+
\beta_{i,L}L_m+\varepsilon_{i,m}.
\tag{13.7}\]
At portfolio formation, the innovations used in this regression are estimated with data available at that date. The liquidity betas are updated at year-end and used during the following calendar year. The factor is the value-weighted return on the highest liquidity-beta decile minus the return on the lowest. We compound the published monthly factor returns beginning in January 1968 and also sum their log returns as in Equation 12.3.

from eap_pl import plot_cumulative_returns

traded = (
    liquidity.filter(pl.col("date") >= pl.date(1968, 1, 1))
    .with_columns(
        compounded=(1 + pl.col("psl")).cum_prod() - 1,
        cumulative_log=pl.col("psl").log1p().cum_sum(),
    )
)
assert traded.select((pl.col("psl").is_finite() & (pl.col("psl") > -1)).fill_null(False).all()).item()
plot_cumulative_returns(traded, y_label="Cumulative liquidity factor return")







Figure 13.3: Compounded and cumulative log returns for the traded liquidity factor, January 1968 to December 2012 (BEM Figure 13.3)





The series ends December 2012 at 701.17% compounded and 208.09% in cumulative log returns.

    traded.select(month="date", psl_pct=100 * pl.col("psl"))

title: 14  Skewness
text:
14.1 Measuring Skewness
Following Chapter 14 of Bali et al. (2016), we measure the asymmetry of past stock returns and ask whether it predicts next month’s return. We examine total skewness, exposure to large market moves, and skewness in the residuals from a factor model.
Total skewness is the third central moment of raw stock returns divided by the second central moment raised to the power \(3/2\). If \(R_{i,s}\) is a return for stock \(i\) and \(\bar R_i\) is its mean in the estimation window, then
\[
\operatorname{Skew}_i=
\frac{n^{-1}\sum_{s=1}^{n}(R_{i,s}-\bar R_i)^3}
{\left[n^{-1}\sum_{s=1}^{n}(R_{i,s}-\bar R_i)^2\right]^{3/2}}.
\tag{14.1}\]
We use the moment formula as written. A constant return series has no defined total skewness.
Co-skewness is the coefficient on the squared market excess return in a regression of stock excess returns.
\[
r_{i,s}=\alpha_i+\beta_i\mathrm{MKT}_s+
\operatorname{CoSkew}_i\mathrm{MKT}_s^2+\varepsilon_{i,s}.
\tag{14.2}\]
The coefficient depends on the units of return. We fit the regression with decimal returns throughout.
Idiosyncratic skewness applies the same moment ratio to mean-zero residuals.
\[
\operatorname{IdioSkew}_i=
\frac{n^{-1}\sum_{s=1}^{n}\hat\varepsilon_{i,s}^{\,3}}
{\left[n^{-1}\sum_{s=1}^{n}\hat\varepsilon_{i,s}^{\,2}\right]^{3/2}}.
\tag{14.3}\]
The residuals come from the Fama–French three-factor regression.
\[
r_{i,s}=\alpha_i+\beta_{i,M}\mathrm{MKT}_s+
\beta_{i,S}\mathrm{SMB}_s+\beta_{i,H}\mathrm{HML}_s+\varepsilon_{i,s}.
\tag{14.4}\]
The formation months are June 1963 through November 2012. The daily windows cover 1, 3, 6, or 12 calendar months and require 15, 50, 100, or 200 observations, respectively. The monthly windows cover 1, 2, 3, or 5 years and require 10, 20, 24, or 24 observations. All windows end in the formation month. The factor regressions match returns to factors at the same frequency and use observations with all the inputs required for that regression. We use the June 2014 archive for the daily and monthly Fama–French factors and the monthly momentum factor.
import polars as pl

from era_pl import load_parquet
from eap_pl import build_book_to_market, build_momentum, build_sizes, get_ff_factors, monthly_panel
from eap_pl._skewness import rolling_skewness

first = pl.date(1963, 6, 1)
last = pl.date(2012, 11, 1)
keys = ["permno", "month"]
daily_windows = {"1m": (1, 15), "3m": (3, 50), "6m": (6, 100), "12m": (12, 200)}
monthly_windows = {"1y": (12, 10), "2y": (24, 20), "3y": (36, 24), "5y": (60, 24)}
windows = daily_windows | monthly_windows

vintage = "201406"
daily_factors = get_ff_factors("daily", vintage=vintage)
monthly_factors = get_ff_factors("monthly", vintage=vintage)

sizes = build_sizes()
monthly_stocks = (
    load_parquet("msf", "crsp")
    .filter(pl.col("date").is_between(first.dt.offset_by("-59mo"), last.dt.month_end()))
    .select("permno", "ret", date=pl.col("date").dt.month_start())
)
formation = (
    monthly_panel(sizes, first, last, monthly_factors=monthly_factors)
    .join(build_book_to_market(sizes).select(*keys, "bm"), on=keys, how="left", validate="1:1")
    .join(build_momentum(first, last).select(*keys, "mom"), on=keys, how="left", validate="1:1")
    .join(monthly_stocks.select(
        "permno", month="date", rev=pl.when(pl.col("ret").is_finite()).then(100 * pl.col("ret")),
    ).collect(), on=keys, how="left", validate="1:1")
)
anchors = formation.select(keys)
daily_stocks = load_parquet("dsf", "crsp").filter(
    pl.col("date").is_between(first.dt.offset_by("-11mo"), last.dt.month_end()),
)

daily_measures = rolling_skewness(anchors, daily_stocks, daily_factors, daily_windows)
monthly_measures = rolling_skewness(anchors, monthly_stocks, monthly_factors, monthly_windows)
We also need the one-month Amihud illiquidity control from Chapter 13. It averages absolute returns per million dollars traded across at least 15 valid days.
illiq = (
    daily_stocks.filter(
        pl.col("date") >= first,
        pl.all_horizontal(pl.col("ret", "prc", "vol").is_finite()),
        pl.col("prc") > 0,
        pl.col("vol") > 0,
    )
    .with_columns(month=pl.col("date").dt.month_start())
    .group_by(keys)
    .agg(illiq=(1e6 * pl.col("ret").abs() / (pl.col("prc") * pl.col("vol"))).mean(),
         days=pl.len())
    .filter(pl.col("days") >= 15)
    .select(*keys, "illiq")
    .collect()
)
panel = (
    formation.join(daily_measures, on=keys, validate="1:1")
    .join(monthly_measures, on=keys, validate="1:1")
    .join(illiq, on=keys, how="left", validate="1:1")
)
families = {"skew": "Total skewness", "coskew": "Co-skewness", "idioskew": "Idiosyncratic skewness"}
labels = {
    family: {f"{family}_{horizon}": f"`{family}_{horizon}`" for horizon in windows}
    for family in families
}
controls = {"beta": "Beta", "log_cap": "Size", "bm": "`bm`",
            "mom": "`mom`", "rev": "`rev`", "illiq": "`illiq`"}

14.3 Correlations
We calculate Pearson and Spearman correlations within each month on observations where both measures are available. For Pearson correlations we winsorize each variable at the 0.5th and 99.5th percentiles. Spearman correlations use the original ranks.

from itertools import combinations

from eap_pl import correlation_matrix, period_correlations, winsorized_corr


def within_family(family):
    terms = labels[family]
    means = (
        period_correlations(panel, terms, "month")
        .select(pl.exclude("month").mean())
        .row(0, named=True)
    )
    return correlation_matrix(means, terms)

The next two tables compare different types of skewness over the same window, then relate each measure to beta, size, book-to-market, momentum, reversal, and illiquidity.

def average_pairs(pairs):
    expressions = []
    for left, right in pairs:
        a, b = pl.col(left), pl.col(right)
        valid = pl.all_horizontal(a.is_finite(), b.is_finite())
        expressions.extend([
            winsorized_corr(a, b).alias(f"Pearson {left} {right}"),
            pl.corr(a.filter(valid), b.filter(valid), method="spearman").alias(f"Spearman {left} {right}"),
        ])
    return (
        panel.group_by("month").agg(expressions)
        .select(pl.exclude("month").fill_nan(None).mean())
        .row(0, named=True)
    )

14.4 Persistence
We pair a stock’s current measure with its value an exact number of months later. We compute the winsorized Pearson correlation across those paired stocks each month, then average across months. We omit lags shorter than the estimation window because the two measures would share returns.

from eap_pl import persistence

lags = [1, 3, 6, 12, 24, 36, 48, 60, 120]


def nonoverlapping_persistence(family):
    terms = labels[family]
    return persistence(panel, terms, lags).with_columns(
        pl.when(pl.col("Lag (months)") >= months)
        .then(pl.col(terms[f"{family}_{window}"])).alias(terms[f"{family}_{window}"])
        for window, (months, _) in windows.items()
    )

title: 14  Skewness
text:
14.5 Skewness and Stock Returns

14.5.1 Univariate Portfolio Analysis
For each measure we form deciles using all eligible stocks with that measure. We compute next-month excess returns, including the delisting adjustments in Section 7.2. Value weights use formation-month market capitalization.
The high-minus-low spread buys the highest-skewness decile and sells the lowest. The four-factor model in Equation 11.2 adds momentum to the three Fama–French factors. FFCPS also includes the traded liquidity factor from Chapter 13. It uses January 1968 through December 2012 because the liquidity factor starts in January 1968. The other models use July 1963 through December 2012. Parentheses show six-lag Newey–West \(t\)-statistics (Newey and West 1987).

from eap_pl import format_fit, hac, load_pastor_stambaugh_2013
from eap_pl._portfolios import assign_portfolio, portfolio_months, spread

momentum_factor = get_ff_factors("momentum", vintage=vintage).select(
    month="date", mom_factor=100 * pl.col("mom"),
)
factors = (
    monthly_factors.select(month="date", mkt=100 * pl.col("mktrf"),
                           smb=100 * pl.col("smb"), hml=100 * pl.col("hml"))
    .join(momentum_factor, on="month", validate="1:1")
    .join(load_pastor_stambaugh_2013().select(month="date", ps=100 * pl.col("psl")),
          on="month", how="left", validate="1:1")
)
specifications = {
    "10–1": "1",
    "FFC α": "mkt + smb + hml + mom_factor",
    "FFCPS α": "mkt + smb + hml + mom_factor + ps",
}
portfolio_tables = {}
spread_estimates = []
for family, terms in labels.items():
    rows = {"EW": [], "VW": []}
    for (term, label), window in zip(terms.items(), windows):
        members = assign_portfolio(panel.filter(pl.col(term).is_finite()), term, 10, "month")
        monthly = portfolio_months(members, ["portfolio"])
        for weight in rows:
            means = monthly.group_by("portfolio").agg(pl.col(weight).mean()).sort("portfolio")
            sample = (
                spread(monthly, 10, 1, "portfolio", weight)
                .select(pl.col("month").dt.offset_by("1mo"), weight)
                .join(factors, on="month", validate="1:1").sort("month")
            )
            fits = {
                name: hac(f"{weight} ~ {rhs}", sample.drop_nulls("ps") if name == "FFCPS α" else sample)
                for name, rhs in specifications.items()
            }
            rows[weight].append({
                "Sort variable": label,
                **{str(decile): value for decile, value in means.iter_rows()},
                **{name: format_fit(fit, "Intercept") for name, fit in fits.items()},
            })
            fit = fits["10–1"]
            spread_estimates.append({
                "measure": families[family], "window": window, "weight": weight,
                "estimate": fit.params["Intercept"], "se": fit.std_errors["Intercept"],
            })
    portfolio_tables[family] = {weight: pl.DataFrame(values) for weight, values in rows.items()}


for table in portfolio_tables["skew"].values():
    show_table(table)

14.5.2 Fama–MacBeth Regressions
For each measure \(X_{i,t}\), we estimate a monthly cross-sectional regression of next-month excess returns. The univariate specification includes only skewness. The full specification is
\[
\begin{aligned}
r_{i,t+1}={}&\delta_{0,t}+\delta_{1,t}X_{i,t}+\delta_{2,t}\beta_{i,t}
+\delta_{3,t}\mathrm{Size}_{i,t}+\delta_{4,t}\mathrm{BM}_{i,t}\\
&+\delta_{5,t}\mathrm{Mom}_{i,t}+\delta_{6,t}\mathrm{Rev}_{i,t}
+\delta_{7,t}\mathrm{Illiq}_{i,t}+\varepsilon_{i,t+1}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{14.5}\]
As in Chapter 13, we take the complete cases for each specification, winsorize the regressors by month at the 0.5th and 99.5th percentiles, and apply six-lag Newey–West inference to the time series of coefficients.

from eap_pl import fama_macbeth_table


def fm_panel(family, controls):
    terms = labels[family]
    result = {"Term": [*terms.values(), *controls.values(), "Intercept", "Adjusted R²", "n"]}
    for index, (term, label) in enumerate(terms.items(), 1):
        regressors = [term, *controls]
        sample = panel.select("month", "excess", *regressors).drop_nulls()
        fit = fama_macbeth_table(sample, [regressors], {term: label} | controls, digits=3)
        values = dict(fit.iter_rows())
        result[f"({index})"] = [values.get(name, "") for name in result["Term"]]
    return pl.DataFrame(result)

title: 15  Idiosyncratic Volatility
text:
15.1 Measuring Total Volatility
We follow Chapter 15 of Bali et al. (2016). We examine whether stocks with more volatile factor-model residuals earn lower returns in the next month, and how the relation changes with portfolio weighting, delisting adjustments, and controls.
Let \(R_{i,s}\) be a decimal stock return, \(n\) the number of observations in the estimation window, and \(m\) the number of periods per year. We use \(m=252\) for daily returns and \(m=12\) for monthly returns. Total volatility is the annualized sample standard deviation, in percent.
\[
\operatorname{Vol}_i = 100\sqrt{m}\,\sqrt{\frac{\sum_{s=1}^{n}(R_{i,s}-\bar R_i)^2}{n-1}}.
\tag{15.1}\]
We also calculate an annualized root mean square using zero in place of the sample mean.
\[
\operatorname{Vol}^{SS}_i = 100\sqrt{m}\,\sqrt{\frac{\sum_{s=1}^{n}R_{i,s}^2}{n}}.
\tag{15.2}\]
crumbs: Part II. The Cross Section of Stock Returns

title: 15  Idiosyncratic Volatility
text:
15.2 Measuring Idiosyncratic Volatility
We regress the stock return in excess of the risk-free rate, \(r_{i,s}\), on factor returns at the same frequency. The Fama–French three-factor model uses market, size, and value returns.
\[
r_{i,s}=\alpha_i+\beta_{i,M}\mathrm{MKT}_s+\beta_{i,S}\mathrm{SMB}_s
+\beta_{i,H}\mathrm{HML}_s+\varepsilon_{i,s}.
\tag{15.3}\]
The CAPM uses the market factor.
\[
r_{i,s}=\alpha_i+\beta_{i,M}\mathrm{MKT}_s+\varepsilon_{i,s}.
\tag{15.4}\]
The four-factor model (FFC) adds momentum.
\[
r_{i,s}=\alpha_i+\beta_{i,M}\mathrm{MKT}_s+\beta_{i,S}\mathrm{SMB}_s
+\beta_{i,H}\mathrm{HML}_s+\beta_{i,U}\mathrm{MOM}_s+\varepsilon_{i,s}.
\tag{15.5}\]
Let \(k\) denote the number of estimated coefficients, including the intercept. Here \(k\) equals 4 for FF, 2 for CAPM, and 5 for FFC.
\[
\operatorname{RSE}_i=\sqrt{\frac{\sum_{s=1}^{n}\widehat\varepsilon_{i,s}^{2}}{n-k}}.
\tag{15.6}\]
Idiosyncratic volatility annualizes the residual standard error and expresses it in percent.
\[
\operatorname{IdioVol}_i=100\sqrt{m}\,\operatorname{RSE}_i.
\tag{15.7}\]
Formation months run from June 1963 through November 2012. Each window ends in the formation month. The daily windows of 1, 3, 6, and 12 months require 15, 50, 100, and 200 observations. The monthly windows of 1, 2, 3, and 5 years require 10, 20, 24, and 24 observations. For factor models, the minimum applies to matched observations. We use CRSP’s reported stock returns to estimate volatility and download the June 2014 vintage of the factors, including daily momentum, with get_ff_factors().

import polars as pl

from era_pl import load_parquet, ptime
from eap_pl import get_ff_factors, load_beta_universe
from eap_pl._volatility import rolling_volatility

first = pl.date(1963, 6, 1)
last = pl.date(2012, 11, 1)
last_holding = last.dt.offset_by("1mo")
keys = ["permno", "month"]
daily_windows = {"1m": (1, 15), "3m": (3, 50), "6m": (6, 100), "12m": (12, 200)}
monthly_windows = {"1y": (12, 10), "2y": (24, 20), "3y": (36, 24), "5y": (60, 24)}
windows = daily_windows | monthly_windows

anchors = load_beta_universe(first, last).sort(keys).collect()
daily = load_parquet("dsf", "crsp").filter(
    pl.col("date").is_between(first.dt.offset_by("-11mo"), last.dt.month_end())
)
monthly = (
    load_parquet("msf", "crsp")
    .filter(pl.col("date").is_between(first.dt.offset_by("-59mo"), last_holding.dt.month_end()))
    .select("permno", "ret", date=pl.col("date").dt.month_start())
    .with_columns(pl.when(pl.col("ret").is_finite()).then("ret").alias("ret"))
)

vintage = "201406"
daily_factors = get_ff_factors("daily", vintage=vintage).join(
    get_ff_factors("momentum_daily", vintage=vintage), on="date", how="left", validate="1:1"
)
monthly_factors = get_ff_factors("monthly", vintage=vintage).join(
    get_ff_factors("momentum", vintage=vintage), on="date", how="left", validate="1:1"
)

with ptime():
    daily_vol = rolling_volatility(anchors, daily, daily_factors, daily_windows, 252)

Wall time: 31.477 s



with ptime():
    monthly_vol = rolling_volatility(anchors, monthly, monthly_factors, monthly_windows, 12)

volatility = daily_vol.join(monthly_vol, on=keys, validate="1:1")

Wall time: 40.393 s


We use the 12-month daily market beta, one-month Amihud illiquidity from Chapter 13, and the five-year monthly co-skewness and idiosyncratic skewness measures from Chapter 14. We use log market capitalization (log_cap), the cumulative return over the preceding 11 months (mom), and the formation-month return (rev) as controls.

from eap_pl import build_book_to_market, build_momentum, build_sizes
from eap_pl._data import monthly_stock_returns
from eap_pl._skewness import rolling_skewness

with ptime():
    usable_days = daily.filter(
        pl.all_horizontal(pl.col("ret", "prc", "vol").is_finite()),
        pl.col("prc") > 0,
        pl.col("vol") > 0,
    ).with_columns(month=pl.col("date").dt.month_start())

    illiquidity = (
        usable_days.filter(pl.col("month") >= first)
        .group_by(keys)
        .agg(illiq=(1e6 * pl.col("ret").abs() / (pl.col("prc") * pl.col("vol"))).mean(),
             days=pl.len())
        .filter(pl.col("days") >= 15)
        .select(*keys, "illiq")
        .collect()
    )

    skewness = rolling_skewness(anchors, monthly, monthly_factors, {"5y": monthly_windows["5y"]})
    sizes = build_sizes()
    betas = load_parquet("betas", "eap").select(*keys, beta="12M")
    adjusted = monthly_stock_returns(first.dt.offset_by("1mo"), last_holding).rename({"ret": "adjusted"})
    holding_returns = (
        monthly.select("permno", month="date", unadjusted="ret")
        .filter(pl.col("month").is_between(first.dt.offset_by("1mo"), last_holding))
        .join(adjusted, on=keys, how="full", coalesce=True, validate="1:1")
        .join(monthly_factors.lazy().select("rf", month="date", market=100 * pl.col("mktrf")),
              on="month", validate="m:1")
        .select("permno", pl.col("month").dt.offset_by("-1mo"), "market",
                excess=100 * (pl.col("adjusted") - pl.col("rf")),
                raw_excess=100 * (pl.col("unadjusted") - pl.col("rf")))
        .collect()
    )

    panel = (
        volatility.join(skewness.select(*keys, "coskew_5y", "idioskew_5y"), on=keys, validate="1:1")
        .join(betas.collect(), on=keys, how="left", validate="1:1")
        .join(sizes.select(*keys, "cap", "log_cap"), on=keys, how="left", validate="1:1")
        .join(build_book_to_market(sizes).select(*keys, "bm"), on=keys, how="left", validate="1:1")
        .join(build_momentum(first, last).select(*keys, "mom"), on=keys, how="left", validate="1:1")
        .join(monthly.select("permno", month="date", rev=100 * pl.col("ret")).collect(),
              on=keys, how="left", validate="1:1")
        .join(illiquidity, on=keys, how="left", validate="1:1")
        .join(holding_returns, on=keys, how="left", validate="1:1")
    )

controls = {
    "beta": "Beta", "log_cap": "Size", "bm": "BM", "mom": "Momentum",
    "rev": "Reversal", "illiq": "Illiquidity",
    "coskew_5y": "Co-skewness", "idioskew_5y": "Idiosyncratic skewness",
}
families = {"vol": "`vol`", "vol_ss": "`vol_ss`", "iv_capm": "`iv_capm`",
            "iv_ff": "`iv_ff`", "iv_ffc": "`iv_ffc`"}
labels = {
    family: {f"{family}_{window}": window.upper() for window in windows}
    for family in families
}

text:
15.4 Correlations
Within each formation month, we use stocks with both measures available and winsorize each variable at the 0.5th and 99.5th percentiles. Each table averages the resulting correlations across months. The square tables put Pearson coefficients below the diagonal and Spearman coefficients above it.

from itertools import combinations

from eap_pl import correlation_matrix


def average_pairs(pairs):
    expressions = []
    for left, right in pairs:
        a, b = pl.col(left), pl.col(right)
        valid = pl.all_horizontal(a.is_finite(), b.is_finite())
        a, b = (x.filter(valid).era.winsorize(prob=0.005, quantile_method="linear")
                for x in (a, b))
        expressions.extend([
            pl.corr(a, b).alias(f"Pearson {left}–{right}"),
            pl.corr(a, b, method="spearman").alias(f"Spearman {left}–{right}"),
        ])
    return (
        panel.group_by("month").agg(expressions)
        .select(pl.exclude("month").fill_nan(None).mean()).row(0, named=True)
    )


def within_family(family):
    terms = labels[family]
    return correlation_matrix(average_pairs(combinations(terms, 2)), terms)


for family in ("vol", "vol_ss"):
    show_table(within_family(family))

15.5 Persistence
We match each stock’s volatility to its value an exact number of months later and average the monthly winsorized Pearson correlations. We omit lags shorter than the volatility window so the two estimates use disjoint sets of returns.

from eap_pl import persistence

lags = [1, 3, 6, 12, 24, 36, 48, 60, 120]
show_table(persistence(panel, iv_labels, lags).with_columns(
    pl.when(pl.col("Lag (months)") >= months).then(pl.col(w.upper())).alias(w.upper())
    for w, (months, _) in windows.items()
))
